findings.finding: Undo can destroy another person's work. UNDO_GRACE_MS=2000 ignores real edits within 2 seconds and compares browser Date.now with server stamps. New-item undos lack kind and skip conflict checking entirely: the local repro deletes an edited new task. Year goals are also classified as task in step(), and latest() has no goals, so their edits are not checked. Rollback writers are unconditional too.
findings.request: Fix with the actual persisted versions after each write and server-conditional update/delete (or an equivalent authoritative conflict guard) covering existing and created tasks/goals/routines and rollback. Do not rely on clock grace or only a pre-read. Add tests for immediate edits, changed newly created records, goal edits and an edit racing between read and write. Until fixed, do not claim whole-set Undo preserves concurrent edits.
findings.additional_path_review: CanvasActivityContext.finishDiff also implements direct-write Undo separately from applyChangeSet: created rows are deleted and c.before fields restored unconditionally, without the later-edit/version guard. Include this direct one-item route in the R1 correction; fixing only card Undo leaves it exposed.

findings.finding: The monetary concurrency claim is incorrect. reserve_ai_provider_call takes a lock but increments only call counts; no money is reserved. Multiple calls admitted sequentially before any provider response all see the same low recorded spend and can collectively overshoot. A four-call allowance concurrency test proves call counts only. record_ai_usage is directly executable by authenticated users and takes arbitrary token/minute values without a reservation identity; a client can poison global spend and deny all households service. Do not test ledger poisoning on production.
findings.request: Correct the evidence claim immediately. Reproduce with isolated fixtures and prepare bounded fixes: server-authoritative usage settlement tied to a unique reservation; pending monetary liability or an explicit bounded exposure policy. Include record failure/missing usage and replay. Keep actual financial limits distinct from estimates. Preserve existing approvals and quota settings.
findings.independent_database_reproduction: Confirmed in disposable real PostgreSQL with production migrations and approved quota values: 16 admitted in-flight calls settled 4800 cents against a 300-cent daily limit. An authenticated client with zero reservations inserted fictitious 30000 cents, after which another household was refused by the global 25000-cent cap.
findings.additional_source_observation: aiUsage.ts usageOf reads only input_tokens/prompt_tokens and output_tokens/completion_tokens, while symphony-agent uses Anthropic ephemeral cache_control. Cache creation/read usage fields are omitted, despite distinct provider prices. Include those and hosted tool charges in reconciliation or explicitly bound/document omitted cost.

Test the callback path, including recovery when a link expires. At minimum keep B05 replay protection explicitly open; don't label this fully verified. No new live account consent needed for isolated tests.

findings.finding: Voice is self-blocking under the committed price and documented approved limits: each connection records 5 minutes x 600 cents = 3000 cents ($30), exceeding both the $3/day and $20/month household limits. Disposable PostgreSQL reproduced first admission allowed followed immediately by symphony-agent monthly_limit. Therefore a voice connection can prevent the first subsequent agent action and later voice starts for that household. This is an internal estimate, NOT an observed $30 provider bill. recordUsage also uses the estimate without checking res.ok, so a failed handshake with a returned HTTP response can record the same estimate.

findings.finding: The R1 3/3 live pass claim includes a false pass: the final report says Thursday Oct 15 but its structured routine_skip targets 2026-10-16 (Friday), against the scenario expected 2026-10-15. findings.finding: Interrupted saves are not proven retry-safe. Local fault injection against actual applyChangeSet committed the first add then lost its response: the function returned reverted:true/kept:[], which the card renders as Nothing was changed. Retrying the exact same two-add card created three fixture rows including a duplicate of the first task. Card creation passes no stable operation/row ID. Separately, direct-create stableRowId includes model-generated title/date spelling; the same user/turn with Call Morgan versus Phone Morgan, or the same instant expressed with -04:00 versus Z, produces different IDs. The endpoint reruns the model on retry rather than replaying an authoritative stored turn result, so same turnId alone is not a complete idempotency guarantee.
findings.request: Add stable persisted operation identities for card Approve and durable replay/deduplication for direct turns, with authorization and exact prior-write preconditions. Distinguish unknown commit outcome from confirmed no-write/rollback; reconcile by operation ID before retry or saying nothing changed. Add regressions for commit followed by lost response, retry/reload of the same card, two devices approving, and model wording/date-format variation on direct retry. Keep hosted interrupted-network proof explicitly pending until exercised on the existing synthetic fixtures. Coordinate with R1 conditional rollback/Undo; do not expand product scope.
